subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: The Cold Chain
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Cold Chain usable.

hook.text: Before refrigeration, meat spoiled in days. Ice was harvested from lakes and shipped worldwide.

buildup.text: The cold chain is a temperature-controlled supply chain for perishables—food, vaccines, chemicals.

discovery.text: Refrigerated ships in the 1880s let Argentina export beef to Europe, creating new global markets.

twist.text: A single break in the cold chain can ruin an entire shipment. Temperature must be constant throughout.

climax.text: COVID vaccines required ultra-cold chains at -70°C. Logistics firms scrambled to build the capacity.

punchline.text: If the chain breaks, so does the product.

quiz.question: What is a cold chain?
options: A chain stored in cold weather
A temperature-controlled supply chain for perishables
